messages:
deploy-bot: publish: py 1.7.0, ts 2.4.0 -> canary
deploy-bot: changelogs: https://artifacts.redwood/releases/2401234567

maya: Heads up — TS canary is breaking imports in a few Next apps. CJS default export missing when bundlers expect it.
sam: Confirmed in CI: failing smoke on example-apps/next. Stacktrace shows `require('redwood-sdk').default` is undefined.
oli: Noticed this too locally. Looks like our rollup export map dropped the `module.exports = default` shim during the new esm-first build.
release-eng: Ok, decision time: block stable promotion, publish a quick patch 2.4.1 with the export shim, and mark 2.4.0 as deprecated. We should avoid unpublishing if we can.
maya: Agreed. Also need customer guidance: tell production users to pin to ts@2.3.x and py@1.6.x until patch lands. We'll update release notes and the status page.
release-eng: Working on the patch now. Plan: bump TS to 2.4.1 with fix, publish to canary first, run smoke, then promote to latest if green. Py is fine but we'll do a 1.7.1 micro to sync changelog (no runtime change).
oli: Quick checklist I'm running through:
```
# build fix
git checkout -b fix/ts-cjs-shim
apply rollup export patch
npm run build:ts
# smoke
npm pack && npm install -g ./redwood-ts-2.4.1.tgz
node ./scripts/smoke-tree-shake.js
```

sam: CI bot, can you run the downstream smoke suite on the patched tarball and report back? @ci-bot
ci-bot: acknowledged. queued job 4821, expected ~12m.
release-eng: Also preparing the registry mitigation commands to avoid accidental promotion:
```
# deprecate bad release
npm deprecate @redwood/sdk@2.4.0 "regression: CJS export broken — use 2.4.1+ or pin to 2.3.x"
# for PyPI add yanked release metadata (can't truly yank without removing, we will post advisory)
twine upload dist/redwood_sdk-1.7.1-py3-none-any.whl --skip-existing
```
maya: I'll draft a small advisory we can paste into release notes and the status page: one short sentence + mitigation steps (pin + ETA). Keep it simple.
release-eng: ETA for 2.4.1 publish: 25–40 minutes (run+verification). If CI fails, we'll rollback promotion and revert canary tag. If patch is green we'll push an emergency changelog entry and notify support.
oli: After publish, important to run `npm dist-tag` check and ensure `latest` isn't accidentally pointed to 2.4.0. If it is, run: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.3.7 latest` as a stopgap.
sam: For internal docs/SDK snippets we should also add a short note under "compat" in README about pinning and how to opt into canary for testing.
release-eng: I'll update the release automation flags to block auto-promote for this PR in the release bot until manual ACK.
ci-bot: downstream job 4821 finished: 14/14 smoke tests passed on patched tarball.
maya: Great — once release-eng publishes 2.4.1 and we run a final quick smoke against example-apps, I'll post the advisory and pin guidance.
release-eng: Published: ts@2.4.1 -> canary, py@1.7.1 -> canary. Pushing to staging for final smoke.
ci-bot: staging smoke suite kicked off (job 4830).
sam: If staging looks good, we will: 1) npm deprecate 2.4.0, 2) promote 2.4.1 to latest, 3) update release notes and support playbook.
maya: I'll coordinate with support to silence alerts and prepare a canned response.
release-eng: Staging smoke clean. Promoting 2.4.1 -> latest now.
deploy-bot: promote: ts@2.4.1 -> latest (run id 9402)
release-eng: Done. Deprecated 2.4.0 on npm with advisory. Py 1.7.1 promoted to latest as well.
maya: Draft posted to #support and status page. Included pin guidance and short timeline.
oli: Closing loop: I've opened a small follow-up PR to add an E2E that checks CJS require path so this doesn't regress.
sam: Thanks everyone. Postmortem note: add a tiny checklist for build changes (export map review). :white_check_mark:
summary: Canary release introduced CJS export regression in TS SDK; team coordinated a quick 2.4.1 republish, deprecation of 2.4.0, pin guidance for customers, and updated release automation to block auto-promote until verification.
